title: RTK Query Mutations and Error Recovery Checkpoint

questions.prompt: A save handler uses await trigger(args) then always shows Saved. A handled 400 still shows success. What fixes the flow?

options.label: Use unwrap with try/catch, or inspect the returned error result explicitly.
Assume every handled RTK error already rejects the ordinary trigger promise.
Set fixedCacheKey so HTTP errors become thrown exceptions.

questions.explanation: Handled errors can be returned in the trigger result; unwrap exposes promise-style rejection. fixedCacheKey shares mutation state and does not alter HTTP error semantics.

questions.prompt: Edit one patches A to B, edit two patches C, then edit one fails. Why is naive undo risky?

options.label: Immer automatically orders all server writes by user intent.
An inverse patch always knows which later request succeeded.
The earlier inverse patch can overwrite newer intent; serialize or reconcile with server state.

questions.explanation: Inverse patches describe local changes, not distributed write ordering. Immer cannot order server operations, and an older patch does not automatically account for later success.

questions.prompt: updateQueryData targets an endpoint/argument with no cached entry. What happens?

options.label: It patches every entry with a matching tag.
It does not create the missing entry; deliberate upsert may be needed.
It automatically starts a GET and creates the result.

questions.explanation: updateQueryData targets an existing exact entry and does not initiate a fetch or patch by tags. upsertQueryData is the explicit creation/replacement mechanism.

questions.prompt: Five requests return 401 together. What is a sensible reauthentication design?

options.label: Coordinate one refresh, retry within a bound, and prevent stale-session credentials from being applied.
Recursively call the refresh wrapper on every 401 without a limit.
Retry every 403 as a token expiry indefinitely.

questions.explanation: Single-flight refresh prevents a stampede and needs session/race cleanup. Recursive unbounded refresh can loop; a 403 usually requires permission handling rather than repeated token refresh.

questions.prompt: A purchase times out after the server may have committed. What is safe?

options.label: Assume timeout guarantees rollback and retry with a new operation ID.
Use fixedCacheKey as the server idempotency token automatically.
Use server idempotency and a reconciliation/status contract before retrying ambiguously.

questions.explanation: A client timeout cannot prove server rollback. Idempotency and reconciliation must be server contracts; fixedCacheKey only controls shared local mutation result state.

questions.prompt: A custom baseQuery catches a network exception. Which result preserves failure semantics?

options.label: Throw every expected transport error without a declared error contract.
Return a typed error result for the UI and lifecycle to handle.
Return an empty data array so callers see success.

questions.explanation: A handled error keeps failure visible and supports predictable endpoint lifecycles. Empty data hides outages as valid results, while uncaught expected exceptions bypass the intended base query contract.
